summary:
The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 amends titles 11 and 28 of the U.S. Code to increase chapter 7 trustee compensation, adjust the allocation of bankruptcy filing fees, modify chapter 11 quarterly fees, extend the term of certain temporary bankruptcy judgeships, and alter the funding structure of the United States Trustee System Fund.

Section 3(a) amends 11 U.S.C. § 330 by striking “$45” in subsection (b)(1) and inserting “$105,” thereby raising the per-case trustee compensation payable from the filing fee. It also strikes subsection (e), which had made the $15 payment under subsection (b)(2) subject to the availability of funds. Together with the unchanged $15 payment under subsection (b)(2), total trustee compensation becomes $120 per case. Section 3(b) directs that, after compensating trustees under 11 U.S.C. § 330(b)(1), the remainder of fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(1)(A) be deposited as follows: $63.51 into the special fund under 28 U.S.C. § 1931; $25.00 into the special fund established by section 10101(b) of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005; and $51.49 into the United States Trustee System Fund under 28 U.S.C. § 589a. Section 3(c) amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a by replacing the percentage-based deposit (40.46 percent of fees) with a fixed amount of $51.49 per case, and by striking subparagraphs (B) and (C) of subsection (f)(1), redesignating subparagraph (D) as (B), and changing “Fourth” to “Second,” thereby revising the distribution priority within the Fund.

Section 4(a) amends 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6)(B) to extend the quarterly fee obligation for chapter 11 debtors from 5 years to 10 years, and to modify the fee calculation by inserting “the greater of” before “0.4” in subclause (I) and increasing the percentage in subclause (II) from 0.8 to 0.9. Section 4(b) amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f) to extend the deposit period for certain fees from 2026 to 2031. Section 4(c) requires that, for fiscal years 2026 through 2031, $5,400,000 of the fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) be deposited into the general fund of the Treasury, with the remainder deposited as specified in section 589a(f).

Section 5 amends section 4 of the Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020 and section 1003(b)(2)(A) of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 2017 (both notes to 28 U.S.C. § 152) by striking “5 years” and inserting “10 years” in each applicable subparagraph, thereby extending the term of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships from 5 to 10 years.

Section 6 provides that the Act generally takes effect on the first day of the calendar quarter on or after enactment. The trustee compensation amendments in section 3 apply to cases under chapter 7, or converted to chapter 7, commenced on or after the October 1 first occurring after enactment. The fee amendments in section 4 apply to chapter 11 cases commenced or pending on the first day of the calendar quarter on or after enactment, and to quarterly fees for disbursements made in any calendar quarter beginning on or after enactment.
